# Independent review: M1A1 damaged-01 localized-impact physical candidate

Job `b6453d0a…` r3 · checkpoint `58038c16…f89eef4` · GLB `855789d8…6cdeb7`. This was read-only and I made no producer calls. Earlier no-gos still stand and nothing was reset.

**Bottom line:** the geometry is clean, but the wound doesn't read as damage at gameplay size. At 256 and 128 this variant looks like the clean tank. My informal recommendation is **no-go** for the damaged-01 visual gate.

## What I looked at
- All six damaged views at 256. At 1000: left, front three-quarter, rear three-quarter, front, right and top. At 128: left.
- The matching clean v1-r2 views at 1000 left and both three-quarters, and at 256/128 left and 256 rear three-quarter.
- The relocation and render manifests, the status file, the export receipt (its tail and producer identity), the d01 feasibility plan, the v48 source audit, `damage-stories-v1`, `source-packet-v6` and the MCO 8420.13 page image.
- Not inspected: the dimension report itself. I only saw its hash, `44e118ce…`, in the status file.

## Findings

**Body identity.** The tank is unmistakably the M1A1 v1.0 base. The audit shows 268 untouched parts with zero vertex, normal and transform change, and identical overall bounds. In the views, the front three-quarter, front, right and top are the same as the clean tank. You were expecting that, but it means **four of six views show no damage at all**.

**Hole, factory opening or missing panel?** It isn't a missing panel: the panel's edges and seam lines are all intact. My strongest objection is that it doesn't read as a hole either:
- **1000 left:** the wound looks like a symmetrical faceted diamond centred between two seams, with a light centre. That reads as a pressed fitting or bolted-on boss, not a torn breach.
- **Why the centre is light:** the opening shows the sand-painted hull 0.69 m behind it. So the through-hole has no dark value to signal depth.
- **Ragged outline:** the planned 6–9 uneven corners don't register at about 25 px of hole width.
- **1000 rear three-quarter:** this is the best view. It reads as a small dark diamond, which could still be taken for a port or bracket.

**Size, depth and rim.** These are designed values, not factory layer measurements, a caliber, or the exact 1991 incident:
- Opening is 0.22–0.30 m (about 25 px at 1000) and the deformed area is 0.55 m (about 50 px).
- The 45 mm rim is about 4 px at 1000 and can't be seen at 256.
- The audit's rays prove the opening goes all the way through to the hull. Visually, though, you can't see the depth from any review view.

**Structural support.** What the audit shows:
- All seven skirt panels are closed and manifold, with no duplicate, boundary or winding errors.
- The 72 retained source faces are intact, the support point sits inside the panel and fender, and the screened track, wheel, hull and accent parts have no new intersections.
- Visually, I see nothing floating or clipping.

Two things remain open:
- The intersection screen is partial, as it says itself.
- It reports 18 left-fender contacts at Z 1.335–1.338. It calls these the unchanged upper interface, but I couldn't confirm the clean tank has the same contacts.

**Gameplay sizes:**
- **256 left:** at most a few pixels differ, and I can't reliably tell the wound from clean seam detail.
- **256 rear three-quarter:** not reliably distinguishable from clean.
- **128 left:** indistinguishable from clean.
- The feasibility plan predicted this risk, and these renders confirm it.

**Damaged vs wreck vs clean.** It's clearly not a wreck: running gear, turret, gun and stance are all intact. The real failure is that it isn't distinguishable from the **clean** tank.

**Source check.** The MCO page (20 Aug 91, Annex V to Appendix W) supports breached skirt surfaces, broken welds and bent skirts. Its replacement threshold is a skirt that "sticks out more than 2 inches". It gives no hole outline or layer details, and on this page the M1A1 tie comes from the surrounding document, not the page itself. The candidate allows at most 10 mm outward displacement (60 mm inward). So the one silhouette-level cue this source documents, an outward-bent skirt, is barely used.

## Rubric (`model-quality` 1.0.0): informal, not an evaluator result
These are scored only where the evidence supports a score. I computed no weighted total and am not asserting an evaluator go.

| Category | Score | Main objection / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Identity & recognition (core) | **1** | M1A1 reads perfectly. The damaged condition doesn't read at 256 in any view, so the variant isn't distinguished from its nearest neighbour (clean). |
| Proportion & mass | 3 (inherited) | Bounds and stance identical to clean. Not newly earned. |
| Silhouette (core) | **2** | Base silhouette is fine. The damage adds nothing to the outline in any view (top and front unchanged). |
| Form hierarchy | 2 | A tertiary-scale detail is being asked to carry the variant's main story. |
| Mechanical coherence (core) | **2** | No structural fault found in the audit or visually. But the through-opening and rim can't be seen in the views, and the collision proof is incomplete. |
| Surface & material | not scored | Weathering unfinished. The opening currently reads as a light boss. |
| Viewpoint robustness | 1 | The weakest four views show a clean tank. |
| Production integrity (core) | not scored | Mask validation still running, so validation isn't current. I didn't inspect the dimension report itself. |

Three core categories score below 3 and a fourth can't be scored, so the core floor fails.

## Kept separate
- **technicalValidation:** Producer validation passed for r3 with 0 issues and deterministic renders (same checkpoint and render hash `32f08dd4…`). Repeat captures are byte-identical at all three sizes. The source audit passes, and you report all 269 parts passing native checks per the producer. The masks are still running, so validation **isn't current**.
- **visualRecommendation:** Informal **no-go** for damaged-01. The structure is sound but the wound doesn't read as damage.
- **humanApproval:** None given or inferred. This isn't a finished asset, no human gate has advanced, and nothing about mobility or weapon operation is claimed.

## Directions, if a further attempt is authorised (not dispatched)
- **Don't just enlarge the hole.** The feasibility plan warns against it.
- **Use the documented bent-skirt cue.** A bounded outward bend of the lower skirt edge would change the outline in the top, front and three-quarter views. The amount is a design choice, and it would need new clearance checks against the track.
- **Give the opening a dark interior.** Apply the planned dark inner-fracture tone to the rim walls. The tan hull behind it currently cancels the sense of depth.
- **Make the outline less symmetrical and less centred** so it doesn't read as a factory fitting, while staying inside the protected margins.

Any further attempt counts against the existing iteration budget.
